problems: The grey powder mark is one even Archimedean spiral. It reads as a snail-shell or hypnosis swirl, not a fingerprint. A print is nested ridge loops that open at the bottom, with their legs running down off the pad. It also renders near-white, not grey powder.
The powder ridges are a thick tube (r 0.0045) with wide gaps, so they read as a coiled wire stuck on the knob instead of a fine dusted print. Use thinner, tighter ridges set close to the surface.
The knob ball shows heavy faceting: a checkered, stepped shading across the sphere. The lathe needs more profile points and more verts so the brass ball reads as smooth and turned.

The door's latch edge (x=0.2) stops short of the casing (x=0.23). The yellow wall shows through the gap as a stray yellow stripe beside the door. The casing should overlap the door edge, the way a stop and casing frame the door.

The fingerprint is nested arches open at the bottom, with two stepped bundles of legs spreading out below. It reads as a Wi-Fi or radio signal symbol, not a fingerprint swirl, and the legs render jagged.
The print has too few ridges with wide gaps, so it looks like wire on the knob rather than a dusted print pad. It needs a dense oval whorl of closely spaced ridges.
